essence: Estimate the camera's ego-motion (pan/yaw, tilt/pitch, roll, forward-translation expansion) for every frame from the fly's direction-selective lobula-plate outputs, then use it for camera motion compensation (CMC/GMC) in the tracker. The Kalman predictions get warped before association, the same way BoT-SORT's sparseOptFlow GMC does it. FlyVis has T4a-d/T5a-d but no HS/VS tangential cells, so the 'HS/VS' stage would be our own matched-filter readout (Krapp/Franz-style flow templates or a ridge decoder) over full-frame tiled T4/T5 activity. The promising variant is not a fly GMC in place of CV GMC. It is a reliability-gated GMC: the fly estimate, or its agreement with DIS/feature GMC, decides when compensation is trustworthy, especially in dark scenes where feature-based GMC fails.

relevance: Registry H1 (motion error: fovea / camera / road decoder). The camera part was never tested with the fly: H1 closed only the per-track directional correction, and H2 found fly residual flow redundant with DIS as a reliability signal. Plan §5 item 3 and §7.1a closed the learned motion model because its gain is absorbed by camera motion compensation, so CMC is the known dominant source of prediction error in road footage (5 Hz/960 protocol). At 30 Hz on val7, BoT-SORT without ReID gave (runs/video_rate/combined/*.json): with sparseOptFlow GMC vs without it, HOTA 54.573 -> 54.639 (+0.12%), IDSw 526 -> 467 (-11.2%), IDF1 60.380 -> 60.320 (-0.10%), tracker time 1.95 -> 22.17 ms/frame. Per video, GMC is worse on 5 of 7 videos, including the darkest one, b1d22449 (HOTA 37.13 -> 35.70, -3.8%), and better on b1cebfb7 (+4.4%) and b251064f (+1.7%). So the topic targets IDSw, the night failure of feature GMC (H9 night drop) and H11 ('functions where the fly is native'). The report's own recommendation is adaptive CMC gated by measurable reliability, and the fly estimate could provide that gate.
novelty_overlap: Self-motion estimation from HS/VS-like matched filters is decades old (Krapp & Hengstenberg 1996; Franz & Krapp 2000) and has many robotic versions: LPTC models, FLIVVER (arXiv 2004.05247), neuromorphic ego-motion on drones (Paredes-Valles et al. 2024). Zhao et al. (2024) already predicted the optic-flow fields of 58 LPTs per hemisphere from connectome T4 layer innervation. CMC in MOT is standard: BoT-SORT GMC (2022), UCMCTrack (AAAI 2024), EscapeTrack (2025, reports BDD100K). The search found no work that reads camera ego-motion out of connectome-constrained FlyVis and feeds it to an MOT tracker's CMC or reliability gate, but that absence proves no novelty. cannot_claim: first bio-inspired ego-motion estimator; first CMC for MOT; that HS/VS neurons are modelled (FlyVis has no LPTCs, the readout is ours); that the fly beats DIS or feature GMC unless it beats the DIS-affine matched control. Also recall H2: fly flow was redundant with DIS for reliability.
author_results: UCMCTrack (AAAI 2024, Table 4, MOT17 val, ByteTrack baseline): HOTA/IDF1 68.43/77.10; +frame-wise CMC 70.97/81.07; UCMC 71.96/82.20; UCMC+CMC 72.97/84.05. DanceTrack val: CMC slightly hurts (HOTA 47.93 -> 47.55). KITTI test (10 Hz driving): adding CMC hurt, with car HOTA 77.1 for UCMCTrack vs 74.2 for UCMCTrack+, which the authors attribute to inaccurate CMC parameters. The tracker runs at >1000 FPS on CPU given detections; MOT17 test UCMCTrack+ HOTA 65.8, IDF1 81.1. EscapeTrack (Signal Processing 2025) claims SOTA on MOT17, MOT20, DanceTrack, SportsMOT and BDD100K with estimated camera parameters on the ground plane [uncertain: BDD100K numbers not retrieved]. Zhao et al. 2024 (anatomy, no video benchmark): 58 LPTs per side, 20 of them HS/VS-type; the VS1 predicted flow field agrees with Calliphora electrophysiology; VS tuning is closer to rotation than translation (minimal error about 26 deg vs 34 deg); downstream neurons pooling several LPTs are more selective. Paredes-Valles et al. 2024: a 5-layer SNN on event-camera input estimates ego-motion and controls a real drone at about 200 Hz (hover, land, sideways manoeuvres); no tracking benchmark. VisualRNet 2026: camera rotation from 80x45 optical flow, mean rotation error 0.315 deg vs 38.68 deg for ORB+RANSAC and 0.804 deg for TartanVO on Deep-FVS; the regression head runs at 729 FPS with 7.7K params, and ORB+RANSAC is reported to fail in a night indoor sequence. Project's own reference at 30 Hz (val7, BDD100K raw video, 5 Hz labels): the GMC numbers given under relevance. Frame rates: MOT17 mostly 30 Hz with moving hand-held and vehicle cameras, DanceTrack 20 Hz static cameras, KITTI 10 Hz vehicle; the drone and VisualRNet work use fast rotations.
measured_level: Biology: neuron response fields. Robotics: ego-motion error and closed-loop flight. MOT (UCMCTrack, EscapeTrack, project BoT-SORT GMC): HOTA/IDF1/IDSw after TrackEval. No external work measures a fly-derived ego-motion estimate at pair (AP) or HOTA level.
matched_control: No external work has a same-information control or a graph null model for the ego-motion readout. UCMCTrack compares none / frame-wise CMC / uniform CMC; VisualRNet compares against ORB+RANSAC and TartanVO. Controls required here: (1) the identical template/ridge readout applied to DIS quarter-resolution flow (880 points per frame, runs/train_cache/*/motion/dis_quarter.npz, already cached for 202 videos), the same-information non-fly baseline; (2) an input-only control: the same readout on temporal differences or a Reichardt EMD over the 721-facet eye input after the retina-lamina front-end; (3) FlyVis with the degree- and sign-preserving shuffled connectome (infrastructure of fly_connectome_null_v1, runs/fly_signatures_null); (4) ultralytics sparseOptFlow and ECC GMC as CV references; (5) the XYWHByteTrack stand without GMC. Earlier project results with similar controls: in H2, fly residual flow added +0.02 AP over geometry but DIS added +0.10 and the fly was indistinguishable from shuffled on top of DIS; the connectome null for signatures showed topology matters (+0.044 AP), but only +0.006 AP over the fly's own input.
conditions_breakdown: External: essentially none for night, overexposure or occlusion. UCMCTrack reports only per dataset; VisualRNet shows a qualitative night indoor example. Project per-video val7 shows GMC is condition-dependent: it hurts on the darkest video (b1d22449, -1.43 HOTA) and helps on b1cebfb7 (+1.97 HOTA). Needed here: the dark (<60/255, 27 dev+test videos) vs bright (43) strata already used in H2 stage B, and a breakdown by camera speed (pan magnitude) and by turning vs straight driving.
cost_here: Data: everything is local (200 train + val7 raw BDD100K videos, YOLO26 detections cached in runs/train_cache/*/detections). Full-frame tiled FlyVis activity (6 tiles x 721 columns x 34 types, including T4a-d/T5a-d) exists only for 8 videos in runs/flyvis_activity (about 19-20 ms/frame on RTX 5070, about 0.27 GB/video float16). Extending it to the 70 dev/test videos costs about 84k frames x 20 ms, roughly 30 min GPU plus about 16 s init per video, so about 50 min wall. Storing only T4/T5, or the template projections directly, avoids about 19 GB. Readout: ridge regression per tile from T4/T5 to 6-8 affine/homography parameters, trained on train videos against pseudo-targets (ECC/sparseOptFlow homographies on full-resolution frames, or a robust affine from DIS). CPU minutes to an hour. Tracker: XYWHByteTrack plus a warp hook on cached detections; warps can be saved as {video}.gmc.npy (the pattern already exists in scripts/confidence_rescue.py). TrackEval on dev/test: CPU, under 1 h. Zero-GPU stage 0: build a DIS-affine GMC from the cached dis_quarter flow and check whether it reproduces sparseOptFlow's +0.12% HOTA / -11% IDSw on val7 and dev/test. That sets the ceiling any fly estimate must reach. Long runs per plan §9 (Start-Process, Idle priority).
expected_effect: Ceiling is small at 30 Hz: GMC gives +0.07 HOTA absolute (+0.12%) and -11.2% IDSw on val7, and is worse on 5 of 7 videos. By H1/H2 precedent, a fly-derived estimate is expected to be at most as good as DIS-affine GMC in daylight: fly flow was redundant with DIS, and constant velocity at 33 ms is already near the prediction ceiling. The only plausible advantage is in the darkest scenes, where feature GMC degrades and the lamina front-end restored the fly signal (+0.009 AP [+0.005; +0.014] night, H2 stage B). Realistic expectation: aggregate HOTA vs stand between 0 and +0.2%, IDSw -5 to -12%; fly-GMC vs DIS-GMC about 0 with a CI through zero; a gated GMC might avoid the -3.8% HOTA loss on the darkest video [uncertain]. No speed gain: tiled fly activity costs about 20 ms/frame, the same as sparseOptFlow GMC (22 ms), unless tiled activity is computed anyway for other heads.
risks: (1) FlyVis contains no HS/VS; the 'HS/VS' stage is our linear decoder, which may do all the work, so the input-only and DIS controls are mandatory. (2) Tiled coverage is coarse (2x3 tiles, about 13.3 px column step), and FlyVis direction representations are stable only over a limited range of apparent scales (Neuroinformatics 2026, 'Range-Limited Scale Stability...'). Large 30 Hz pans of 20+ px/frame may exceed T4/T5 velocity tuning or alias; evaluate stratified by pan speed. (3) Road scenes: forward translation creates depth-dependent flow, so one homography is wrong for near objects, and independently moving vehicles contaminate the global estimate; detections must be masked. (4) Pseudo-targets from ECC/feature GMC are themselves unreliable at night, exactly where the fly should help. BDD100K GPS/IMU 'info' files would give an independent reference but need a separate data download, which requires user permission. (5) Project rules: the detector stays frozen (satisfied); compare only one condition at a time (fly-GMC vs DIS-GMC vs sparseOptFlow under the same tracker); no gain claims without per-video bootstrap CI; signs from short runs are not transferred to full runs; negative results are not novelty.
attribution: Ours: the readout of frozen FlyVis T4/T5 activity into camera-motion parameters ('HS/VS-like matched-filter readout', not 'HS/VS neurons'), its use as CMC or as a reliability gate for CMC in XYWHByteTrack, and the matched controls. Borrowed and cited: FlyVis model and weights (Lappalainen et al. 2024); the matched-filter/LPTC concept (Krapp & Hengstenberg 1996; Franz & Krapp 2000); LPT flow-field maps (Zhao et al. 2024) if used as templates; the GMC procedure (BoT-SORT, ultralytics GMC); CMC evaluation practice (UCMCTrack 2024).
